# 10 pro tips to boost your restaurant’s SEO

*   Share
*   [![](https://get.grubhub.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/facebookfb.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://get.grubhub.com/blog/restaurant-seo/)

When a customer searches Google for local restaurants, they see a few results: a Google map, business listings, and articles about local restaurants. As a restaurant owner, your goal is to show up in as many of these places as possible. That’s where restaurant search engine optimization (SEO) comes in — it helps your restaurant website rise to the top of the Google search results, boosting brand visibility and bringing in more traffic.

New to restaurant SEO? Let’s explore how it works and identify ways to improve your search ranking.

## **What is SEO, and why do restaurants need it?**

SEO is the process of building and refining your restaurant website to make it more visible to customers in search results. An SEO [marketing strategy](https://get.grubhub.com/blog/restaurant-marketing-strategy/) is usually tailored to Google’s guidelines — after all, [90.8% of all online queries](https://www.oberlo.com/statistics/search-engine-market-share) go through this search engine.

When you perform basic restaurant [SEO marketing](https://get.grubhub.com/blog/local-store-marekting-ideas/), you make sure the content on each page of your website is focused on a specific keyword. The keyword is the phrase people are most likely to type into Google: “restaurants near me,” “best Italian restaurant in Los Angeles,” or “vegan restaurants in Chicago,” for example.

Content is just one part of search engine optimization. It also involves:

*   **Technical site elements.** These factors include load time, mobile usability, security, and information architecture.
*   **Page elements.** On-page elements can include header structure, metadata, URLs, title tags, schema, and image and video placement.
*   **Backlinks.** Google assesses the websites that link to your pages for authority, quality, and relevance. It also notes links between your website and your social media profiles, podcast, online store, YouTube channel, [Google Business Profile](https://get.grubhub.com/blog/google-business-for-restaurants/), and other digital assets.
*   **Adherence to Google guidelines.** The search algorithm determines how well your site aligns with [Google’s recommendations](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content).

When your site is optimized correctly and thoroughly, it’s easier for Google to show it in relevant local search results. That way, when a customer types in “best Indian restaurant in Cleveland,” your business will be right there at the top of the list.

It’s hard to underestimate the importance of a high ranking — it helps you get more traffic, reach more customers, and build brand awareness. And when an existing patron comes looking for your online menu or current operating hours, they can find what they need quickly. 

## **10 tips to improve your restaurant SEO**

Restaurant SEO sounds technical, but many steps are actually relatively simple. If you know how to edit your website, you have all the skills you need to get started today. After that, you can look to a restaurant SEO services company to handle technical SEO.

As you start optimizing, keep in mind that Google measures searches based on [five key factors](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/ranking-results/):

*   **Meaning.** What’s the intent behind the search? What exactly is the user looking for?
*   **Relevance.** Is your content relevant to the person’s search? Does it match both the intent and the keywords?
*   **Quality.** Is your content helpful, original, and trustworthy? Can Google tell that you’re a legitimate business? Do other authoritative websites link to your content?
*   **Usability.** Is the page easy to navigate? Does it load quickly? Does it perform well on mobile devices?
*   **Context.** Is your content relevant to the searcher’s location, search history, and search settings? This is critical for restaurants because local business searches are typically based on the user’s location or location-based keywords.

Now that you have a sense of what Google’s looking for, it’s time to adjust your [restaurant website](https://get.grubhub.com/blog/restaurant-website-tips/) accordingly. Start improving your restaurant SEO with these helpful tips.

### **1\. Pick relevant keywords**

Your keywords are the foundation of your SEO strategy — make sure they match what your current and potential customers are actually searching for. Common restaurant keywords include:

*   Cuisine type + city or neighborhood
*   Cuisine type + “near me”
*   Restaurant name
*   “Restaurants near me”
*   “Restaurants with delivery/online ordering near me”
*   “Best restaurants” + city
*   Restaurant concept + city
*   Dining area type (rooftop, outdoor, dog-friendly, candlelit, etc.) + city

For some businesses, local keywords are pretty straightforward; for others, they can be more complicated. Customers probably won’t search for “Asian fusion restaurant in Chicago” — instead, they might type in “Asian restaurant in the Loop” or “Japanese food on the Magnificent Mile.”

Here’s the most important thing: Don’t try to optimize for every keyword you can think of. Pick a few to focus the content on for each page. Typically, the most important areas to focus on are the city and neighborhood, cuisine type, restaurant concept (diner, family restaurant, fine dining, etc.), and signature dishes. If you have an outstanding feature, such as a Michelin star or a rooftop lounge, you can also create pages with those keywords.

In a large market, you might need to use more specific keywords to stand out. In addition to “Thai restaurant New York City,” add more focused terms such as “authentic Thai dumplings West Village” or “Thai restaurant handmade rice noodles Chelsea.” Tools such as [Google Keyword Planner](https://ads.google.com/home/tools/keyword-planner/) can be a good place to start your keyword research; [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console/about) and Google Analytics help you discover how customers are currently finding your website.

# Taste The Traffic: Boosting Restaurant Rankings With SEO

[Feb192024](https://imarketing.my/2024/02/19/ "12:00 pm")

[SEO](https://imarketing.my/category/blogs/seo/)

In the past, a restaurant in Malaysia could thrive by serving delicious dishes and providing top-notch customer service.  Word-of-mouth would spread, and soon,  the restaurant became a local favourite.

However, times have evolved. Today, the projected growth for Malaysia’s food service industry is remarkable, and it’s expected to reach [23.95 billion USD by 2029](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/malaysia-foodservice-market#:~:text=The%20Malaysia%20Foodservice%20Market%20size,period%20\(2023%2D2029\).), growing at a CAGR of 12.89%. This growth is promising for restaurants as it means more and more Malaysians are dining out. Besides, it signifies increased competition as new restaurants continue growing nationwide. Moreover, the competition has gotten even tougher because of social media and Google’s search engine changes.

When customers leave good reviews and post yummy food photos on social media like Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook, it helps a restaurant become well-liked. Yet, one negative review can also hurt a restaurant’s business. Google Search and social media have the power to either boost or harm a restaurant’s image and how well it does. 

This is why restaurants must have a smart SEO plan to shine in the busy world of social media and the internet. The restaurant’s SEO strategy includes ensuring all the details about the restaurant are accurate in online listings, enhancing the restaurant’s website, and handling social media platforms and other online channels. This article will explore different ways a restaurant can use SEO.

## What Is SEO For Restaurants?

**SEO for restaurants** is restaurant search engine optimization, which is about making your restaurant’s website appear better when people search for food online, like in Google. Restaurant SEO is a way to ensure more hungry folks discover your eatery online.

Here’s how it works: First, you find the words people use when they search for places to eat. Next, you use those words on your website. This makes your restaurant’s site appear higher in search results when people use those words.

Also, ensuring your website looks nice and functions well on mobile phones is important. Plus, your restaurant should be easy to find on maps and local searches. All these things make your restaurant more visible online.

So, **restaurant SEO** aims to use these tricks to stand out from other restaurants, reach more people, and get more hungry customers to visit your place.

## Why Restaurant SEO Matters

In today’s world, where people rely on search engines and online food orders, ensuring your restaurant’s website is well-optimised is crucial. Restaurant SEO is important for several key reasons:

### 1\. Boosted Visibility:

When you have a strong SEO strategy, your restaurant’s website appears higher in search engine results. This means more people can find you when looking for places to eat. Being the top result on Google, it gets about 33% of all the clicks, so it’s a big deal.

### 2\. More Organic Visitors: 

SEO brings organic (unpaid) visitors to your website, so you’re not relying on paid ads. For most businesses, including restaurants, more than half of the people who visit their restaurant websites do so through organic search, which means effective SEO can bring a lot of visitors.

### 3\. Improving User Experience:

SEO includes making your website simpler to use, faster to load, and more suitable for mobile devices. These changes create a more enjoyable experience for visitors. To give you an idea, Google learned that over half of people using their mobile phones will leave a webpage if it doesn’t load within three seconds.

### 4\. Local Search And Mobile Optimization: 

Since restaurants serve local customers, optimising for local searches is crucial. A lot of people search for things like “restaurants near me.” Also, since many people use their mobile phones to surf the web, your website must function on phones. In fact, over half of all the web traffic globally comes from mobile devices.

## 7 Steps To Boost Your Restaurant’s Online Visibility

### Step 1: Set Your SEO Goals

Before diving into the world of improving your restaurant’s online presence, starting with a clear plan is essential. Consider it setting your restaurant’s online compass in the right direction. Here’s how you can do it:

*   Know Your Audience: Begin by understanding who your ideal customers are. What do they like? Where are they from? What kind of food are they looking for? Knowing your audience helps you fine-tune your online strategies to reach the right people.
*   Set Specific Targets: Decide on specific, measurable goals. For example, you might want to increase the number of people visiting your website, boost your search engine rankings, or generate more online food orders. Having these targets makes it easier to track your progress and adjust your strategies as needed.
*   Highlight What Makes You Unique: What makes your restaurant stand out? Is it your special dishes, the cosy atmosphere, or a unique location? Tailor your SEO goals to emphasise these unique features. This way, you’ll attract customers who appreciate what’s special about your place.
*   Think Local: If your restaurant serves a specific area, you must focus on local search. More and more people search for things like “restaurants near me.” So, it’s essential to tailor your SEO efforts to capture the attention of locals and appear in relevant local Google search results.
*   Set a Timeline: Achieving your SEO goals takes time. It’s an ongoing process. Yet setting up milestones and deadlines helps you stay on track and keeps you motivated.
